title: Do Deterministic Verifiers Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Paired Shared‑Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) to measure whether coupling a deterministic NetOps verifier and deterministic accept/reject gate (generate→validate→repair, max 1 automated repair) to a single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) changes safety outcomes when the identical initial LLM candidate is observed with and without gating under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We evaluated 200 deterministically selected paired intents in a sandboxed Batfish‑style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). All 200 shared initial candidates passed validation in both baseline and guarded arms (contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered paired estimand (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0; exact two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). No automated repairs were applied. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the paired contrast isolates only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates and does not measure effects due to additional guarded‑conditioned regeneration, prompt engineering, or multiple independent samples. We present the preregistered design, implementation and execution accounting, artifact‑grounded interpretation of the null result, and concrete artifact‑supported recommendations for follow‑up designs that avoid ceiling effects.

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are increasingly proposed to translate high‑level operator intent into network device configurations and maintenance workflows. Operational deployment requires evidence that model outputs will not introduce reachability, isolation, or policy violations when applied to live networks. Prior surveys and empirical reports emphasize that operational trustworthiness depends strongly on surrounding system machinery—retrieval, deterministic validators, gates, and repair loops—rather than the model alone [1]–[3]. Architectures that combine generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair (generate→validate→repair) have been widely proposed as a path to safer automatic changes, but reproducible paired evidence that isolates the verifier/gate effect on identical model candidates is limited.

Research question. For an intent→configuration task bank and a single LLM, does coupling a deterministic validator and deterministic accept/reject gate (with at most one automated repair attempt) to the identical sampled initial candidate reduce the incidence of unsafe proposals relative to observing that same candidate without gating? We formalized this question as the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired design and frozen execution (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) that fixed generation semantics, sampling, model, validator, gating policy, and analysis prior to observation; (2) an autonomous confirmatory run using gpt‑5‑mini and a Batfish‑style deterministic validator on n=200 deterministically selected paired intents with shared_initial_candidate semantics; (3) artifact‑grounded analysis showing complete concordance (all candidates valid) and no repair activity; (4) an interpretation of this degenerate null grounded in archived artifacts; and (5) concrete, artifact‑supported recommendations for follow‑up preregistered designs that avoid ceiling effects and permit nondegenerate inference of verifier/gate value.
sections.related_work:
Recent work explores LLM assistance in NetOps/AIOps tasks including intent→config translation, runbook generation, RCA, and agentic automation prototypes [1]–[4]. Surveys and empirical reports document hallucination and unsafe command risks in operational contexts and argue for validator‑coupled pipelines, RAG anchoring, and external safety checks [2],[3].

Cross‑domain evidence. Generate→validate→repair architectures are advocated across domains (program repair, DevOps, verification). In related fields, empirical studies and prototypes show that combining generation with deterministic checks or repair loops can reduce observable defects or aid repairability under the specific datasets and validators used in those studies [5],[6]. These cross‑domain results motivate controlled, reproducible NetOps evaluations but do not imply universal effectiveness: reported gains depend on dataset composition, validator coverage, and experimental protocol.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. The study was preregistered as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 and fixed the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate; model/adaptor = gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and gate policy; repair budget = 1 automated repair attempt per intent; task selection rule and sample size = 200 paired intents; and the confirmatory analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1. The preregistration preceded data collection and is archived.

Generation semantics clarification (preregistered and executed). The executed and preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded arms per paired intent. Therefore the confirmatory estimand evaluates only validator/repair/gate effects on that same first‑pass candidate and does not measure any effect of guarded‑conditioned regeneration or model sampling variance.

Model configuration and determinism note. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini. The recorded model configuration field temperature = null (execution artifact). Null or unset temperature in the recorded configuration is not evidence of deterministic model sampling (it is not equivalent to temperature=0); the adapter produced exactly one sampled generation per pair and the adapter does not guarantee deterministic sampling. This sentence is an explicit methodological clarification: no claim of deterministic model sampling is made.

Task bank, validator, and scoring. Tasks: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced intent→configuration items containing required_sequence lists and workflow_policies (final_group and minimum_up constraints, protected interfaces). The deterministic sampler selected 200 paired intents by a preregistered index rule. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements sequencing and precondition checks, group/availability constraints, and reachability/policy consistency; the primary binary outcome unsafe_flag indicates any post‑candidate reachability or workflow/policy violation. Intervention arms: Baseline observes the shared initial candidate with no gating; Guarded applies the deterministic validator and a deterministic gate that allows up to one automated repair attempt when violations are detected (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Repair attempts, when applied, used the same model under the preregistered repair prompt budget; repair traces are archived when present.

Confirmatory analysis. The primary confirmatory analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 comparing the binary unsafe_flag between baseline and guarded across pairs. The test produced discordant pair counts n10 (guarded_only) and n01 (baseline_only), an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent p‑value, and a paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000). Missingness policy = complete_pair_primary with a one‑retry rule for infrastructure errors.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run executed under the preregistered plan: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Provider audit showed 200 completed hosted model calls and no provider retries. No cross‑condition regeneration occurred because of shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) is n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Thus every shared initial candidate was scored VALID_CONFIGURATION by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in both arms. The preregistered paired estimand (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0. Exact two‑sided test p = 1.0. Paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). The zero‑width CI and p = 1.0 directly reflect absence of discordant pairs under the registered estimand and analysis procedure.

Repair activity and diagnostics. repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes; no automated repairs were invoked. Representative episodes show parsed_command_count == required_command_count and validator violation_count = 0. Task difficulty metadata in the archived manifest indicates most items labeled 'very_hard' with a minority labeled 'extreme'; exact per‑label counts are available in the archived task manifest.

Latency and operational notes. Because only a single generation per pair was produced, model_call accounting equals 200; the guarded pipeline added deterministic validator execution time but no repair cycles. Median per‑pair wall time was dominated by validator evaluation; full timing distributions are archived for reproducibility.

Missingness and contamination. All preregistered exclusion and contamination checks were exercised; no pairs were excluded and contamination flags were not raised. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed and completed_pair_count = 200.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded interpretation of the degenerate null. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the confirmatory estimand isolates only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates. Observing n11 = 200 implies that, for the chosen model (gpt‑5‑mini), the selected synthetic task bank, the prompt/template family used, and the validator ruleset, the sampled initial candidates already satisfied the validator constraints; therefore the guarded machinery applied no repairs and caused no acceptance changes. The archived artifacts (paired contingency and per‑episode validator traces) support this interpretation.

Why the paired bootstrap CI is degenerate. With no discordant pairs every bootstrap resample of paired outcomes yields the same paired difference (0.0); empirical variance is zero and the percentile bootstrap CI is [0.0,0.0]. This is an inferentially valid outcome of the preregistered estimator and analysis executor rather than an analysis malfunction.

Contributors to the ceiling effect (artifact‑traceable). The artifacts point to three concrete contributors: (1) task‑bank alignment — required_sequence and workflow_policies in the task generator matched the expected prompt schema and increased the probability of syntactically correct outputs; (2) validator coverage — the deterministic validator encoded sequencing and precondition checks closely aligned to the synthesized reference answers so correctly formatted model outputs passed validation readily; and (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics — preventing any guarded‑conditioned regeneration or sampling variance removed a mechanism by which the guarded arm could have differed from baseline. Each contributor is traceable in the archived task manifest, validator traces, and model configuration artifacts.

Design recommendations grounded in execution artifacts. To measure verifier/gate value under nondegenerate conditions we recommend: (a) augmenting the task bank with adversarial or out‑of‑distribution intents to raise baseline unsafe rates (the task generator supports seed modification and adversarial seed injection); (b) executing a confirmatory design that uses independent generation per condition (two independent model calls per pair) or multiple independent samples per condition to capture guarded‑conditioned regeneration and model sampling variance (this increases model_call accounting accordingly); (c) testing multiple model variants or explicit sampling temperatures to expose model variance effects; (d) increasing the automated repair budget or enabling iterative repair loops when initial violations are nontrivial; and (e) including human‑in‑the‑loop arms to assess operator responses to validator flags. These recommendations follow directly from the archived configuration and execution artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing an LLM‑alone observation to the same initial candidate after deterministic verification and bounded automated repair. Every sampled initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator and the guarded pipeline applied no repairs; the paired difference = 0.0 (p = 1.0) with paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]. This null result is specific to the chosen model (gpt‑5‑mini), the synthetic task bank, the validator ruleset, and the shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not contradict prior evidence that validators can reduce unsafe outputs under different experimental regimes (e.g., independent per‑condition generation, adversarial inputs, multiple model samples) [1]–[3],[5],[6]. We archive full artifacts and recommend follow‑up preregistered designs that intentionally increase baseline unsafe rates or permit independent per‑condition generation to quantify verifier/gate contributions under more challenging conditions.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration and autonomy: the study was preregistered as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 and executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Models and tools: single LLM = gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); orchestration/adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Human role and autonomy boundary: the human Research Director selected the topical family and constrained the initial prompt before the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer‑review emulation, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the lock. Generation semantics clarification: the executed and preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation was produced and reused by both arms per pair); therefore the confirmatory estimand measures only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates rather than effects from guarded‑conditioned regeneration or multiple independent model samples. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The full execution and analysis artifact bundle (including raw generations, validator traces, task manifest, and archived analysis results) is archived and available as the study's evidence bundle under the preregistration id.
limitations: Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics mean baseline and guarded conditions began from an identical initial candidate; the confirmatory estimand therefore measures only validator/repair/gate effects on that same candidate and cannot assess effects of guarded‑conditioned regeneration or sampling variance.

Construct validity: tasks were synthetic and deterministically selected; the binary unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage (reachability and workflow sequencing rules) and may not capture all operational risks (transient performance regressions, vendor‑specific side effects outside validator rules).

External validity: single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions.

Conclusion validity: the observed null effect (paired difference = 0) reflects this execution's sampling frame where baseline generation produced only valid candidates; the study was powered to detect ~10 percentage‑point reductions per preregistration but cannot rule out smaller effects under different sampling or adversarial inputs.
Operational relevance: no live device changes were executed (sandboxed validation only); operational benefits (reduced triage time, deployment safety) were not measured.
Security/contamination: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; no retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) was used, so retrieval‑based poisoning vectors were not evaluated.

Task‑bank reporting: the archived task_manifest contains exact per‑label counts and is authoritative for difficulty‑label distributions; the manifest indicates most items labeled 'very_hard' with a minority labeled 'extreme'.
